files.title: File explorer
files.sharesDesc: Regular user sessions can't read the OMV shared folder list, so the list read when an administrator signs in is kept as labels. File system permissions decide what can actually be opened, and you can also apply OMV shared folder privileges below.
files.refreshFailed: Couldn't read the shared folder list.
files.showDisksDesc: Lets administrators see outside shared folders, up to the top of the disks under /srv.
files.trashDesc: The top of an OMV data disk is usually owned by root, so users can't create a trash there. Creating a disk trash puts a .Trash folder (1777) shared by all users at the top of the disk, and trash-put on the server uses the same trash. Creating it requires root elevation.
files.followPrivilegesDesc: Applies the shared folder privileges set in OMV to the file explorer as well. Shared folders without access are hidden, and read-only shared folders can't be written to. File system permissions still apply, and administrators follow their own account's privileges too. After changing privileges, press “Read now”.
files.followPrivilegesFallback: This doesn't take effect until the shared folder list has been fetched.
files.followFailed: The shared folder list couldn't be fetched, so privileges weren't turned on.

loginScreen.intro: These settings apply to the sign-in screen for everyone. You can see the result after signing out.

loginScreen.easterEggDesc: Shows an animation when the sign-in screen is left idle for 30 seconds.

defaultScreen.intro: Applied to users who haven't chosen their own theme or wallpaper in Screen settings.

server.intro: Settings that Onmaru runs with. The values in the first section can be changed here; the rest are set in the server's settings file.
server.invalid: The value isn't in a valid format.
server.editableDesc: Takes effect immediately and overrides the value from the settings file.
server.workbenchDesc: Address the browser uses to open the OMV web UI. Leave empty to hide the OMV Workbench app.
server.smartDesc: SMART information is read again once a day after this time (server time).
server.terminalDesc: Lets accounts that can sign in over SSH open a shell from the dashboard. Who can sign in is still decided by OMV's SSH settings.
server.runtimeDesc: Values the server started with and where they came from.
server.howToDesc: These values are environment variables in /etc/default/maru. Restart the service after editing. If you change the listen address, update the reverse proxy too.
server.howToInstall: You can also run ./install.sh --reinstall again from the repository and answer its questions.

helper.title: Privileged helper
helper.desc: A separate service running as root lets Onmaru act with your own Linux account and, after you enter your password again, with root rights for a few minutes.

stateDesc.disabled: Run ./install.sh --reinstall again and choose to install the helper.
stateDesc.unavailable: Onmaru can't reach the helper. Check systemctl status maru-helper.socket on the server.
stateDesc.none: The helper didn't accept this account when you signed in (for example a system account, or it was unreachable). Signing in again retries.
stateDesc.reauth: The helper restarted and no longer knows this session. Sign out and sign in again.
stateDesc.active: This session can use the helper.

helper.rootDesc: Needed by some administrator features. Ends automatically after 5 minutes.
helper.notAllowed: This account can't elevate. It must be in openmediavault-admin and in the helper's elevate group (sudo by default).

update.intro: Check the git repository Onmaru was installed from for a new version, and upgrade to it.

disabled.title: Upgrading from the dashboard is off
disabled.notEnabled: Run this in the repository as its owner to turn it on.
disabled.noHelper: This needs the privileged helper. Run this in the repository as its owner to install both.
disabled.stateDir: Not available when the state directory has been moved from its default location (/var/lib/maru).
disabled.how: The repository must be cloned by a regular account, not root.

update.checkDesc: Checking changes nothing. A remote check looks at the tracked branch, and a local check looks at the current checkout.
update.pending: Check requested. Waiting for it to start…
update.stalled: The upgrade service is not picking up the request. On the server, check that maru-upgrade.path is running.
update.interrupted: The upgrade service seems to have stopped midway. See the log in journalctl -u maru-upgrade, then check again.
update.checkFailedDesc: Nothing was changed. The full log is in journalctl -u maru-upgrade.
update.outdated: The installation changed after this check. Check again.
update.manualDesc: This version can't be installed from the dashboard because:
update.manualHow: Sign in over SSH as the repository owner and run:
update.manualHowUser: Sign in over SSH as the repository owner ({{user}}) and run:
update.manualPull: If the repository doesn't have the new version yet, run git pull first. After one manual upgrade, later versions can be upgraded here again.
update.questionsDesc: These settings must be set before upgrading. Other settings stay as they are.
update.reasonInvalid: the current value can't be used by the new version
update.answerInvalid: Use letters, digits and symbols without spaces (up to 512 characters).
update.notesAfter: After upgrading, please do the following.
update.applyDesc: You need to enter your password again. When the upgrade finishes, Onmaru restarts and everyone is signed out.
update.confirmMessage: The new version is built and installed, and everyone is signed out when it finishes. Check the commit list before you continue.
update.cannotElevate: This account can't elevate to root. Sign in with an account in both openmediavault-admin and the elevation group (sudo by default).
update.noHelperTicket: This session cannot use the privileged helper. Sign out and sign in again with a Linux account.
update.applyingDesc: When it finishes, Onmaru restarts, and this page reloads once it reconnects.
update.applyWaiting: Upgrade requested. Waiting for it to start…
update.applyFailedDesc: The installed version is unchanged. Fix the cause, then check again.
update.applyFailedInstall: The new version could not be installed. If the dashboard misbehaves, run ./install.sh in the repository over SSH to recover.

errors.busy: A check or upgrade is already in progress.
errors.disabled: Upgrading from the dashboard is not available.
errors.outdated: Things changed after the check. Check again.
errors.elevationNotAllowed: This account cannot elevate to root.
errors.helperReauth: The privileged helper forgot this session. Sign out and sign in again.
errors.helperUnavailable: The privileged helper is not available.
errors.badRequest: A setting value is not valid.

readOnly.system: This is a built-in OMV system account, so its email and tags can't be changed.
readOnly.locked: Changes to this account are disabled in OMV.

profile.saveConfigDirty: Not saved: OMV has changes that haven't been applied yet. Apply them in the OMV web UI first.
profile.saveApplyFailed: Your account information was changed, but applying it in OMV failed. Apply it in the OMV web UI.

profile.omvHintSystem: The built-in OMV administrator account isn't listed in OMV user management.

profile.omvHintUser: An administrator can change your password and other account details in the OMV web UI.
profile.tagsDesc: Same as Tags in OMV user management. Separate tags with a comma or Enter.

profile.invalid: Check the email address and tags.

profile.saveDescUser: After saving, an administrator applies the pending change in the OMV web UI.

security.intro: Sensitive features can ask for a second step. Manage your passkeys, authenticator app and recovery codes here.
security.sessionDesc: The check lasts until you sign out or the session expires.
security.assuranceLoginDesc: Signed in with a password only. Signing in does not count as a password check.
security.assurancePasswordDesc: You entered your password again in this session.
security.assuranceTwoFactorDesc: You confirmed with a passkey, an authenticator app or a recovery code.
security.passkeysDesc: Confirm with this device’s screen lock or a security key. This is the recommended method.
security.passkeysOff: Passkeys are not available because the administrator has not set the public address (MARU_PUBLIC_ORIGIN).
security.passkeysUnsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys at this address. Passkeys need HTTPS with a trusted certificate.
security.deviceCode: Add a passkey on another device
security.deviceCodeDesc: Creates a code to enter when you confirm your identity on a new device that does not have this device’s passkey. It works once within 10 minutes.
security.deletePasskeyMessage: You will not be able to confirm with this passkey anymore.
security.passkeyLogins: Browsers that sign in with a passkey
security.passkeyLoginsDesc: Browsers where this is on sign you in with a passkey instead of your password. Turn it on in each browser; it works for {{days}} from the day you turn it on.
security.disablePasskeyLoginMessage: That browser will need your password to sign in until you turn this on again.
security.passkeyLoginHereOn: On. Turning it on again restarts the period from today.
security.totpDesc: Enter a 6-digit code from an app such as Google Authenticator or 2FAS.
security.deleteTotpMessage: You will not be able to confirm with codes from this app anymore.
security.recoveryDesc: One-time codes for when you lose your passkey or phone. They are created with your first method.
security.recoveryNeedsMethod: Add a passkey or an authenticator app first.
security.regenerateMessage: Your current recovery codes will stop working.

securityPolicy.intro: Choose which check sensitive features need. The check stays with the session until it ends.
securityPolicy.invalid: The security policy was not accepted.
securityPolicy.levelsDesc: Password again asks for the password once more in the session. Two-step verification needs a passkey, an authenticator app or a recovery code, or OpenMediaVault two-factor sign-in.
securityPolicy.elevationDesc: Before an administrator elevates to root.
securityPolicy.filesDesc: Before browsing folders or downloading and uploading files in the file explorer.
securityPolicy.noAutoLogout: OpenMediaVault auto logout is off, so a checked session stays checked until sign-out. Turn on auto logout in the OMV web UI.
securityPolicy.passkeysOff: Set the public dashboard address (MARU_PUBLIC_ORIGIN in /etc/default/maru, or ./install.sh --reinstall) to use passkeys. Authenticator apps work without it.
securityPolicy.passkeyLoginDaysDesc: The period is counted from the day it is turned on in a browser. A shorter period applies right away to browsers that already have it on; a longer one applies only to browsers that turn it on afterwards.
securityPolicy.usersDesc: Reset the methods of a user who lost them. Their sessions end, and they can register new methods after signing in again.
securityPolicy.noUsers: No user has registered a method yet.
securityPolicy.unreadable: The record cannot be read. Reset it to start over.
securityPolicy.resetMessage: All passkeys, the authenticator app and the recovery codes of {{user}} will be removed, and their sessions will end.
securityPolicy.filesScopeDesc: If applied to writes and deletions only, browsing folders and downloading need no check, and the check is asked only before uploading, creating, renaming, moving, deleting, and trash operations.

stepUp.title: Security check
stepUp.passwordHint: Enter your password again to continue.
stepUp.totpHint: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
stepUp.recoveryHint: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each code works only once.
stepUp.manageHint: To change your sign-in methods, enter your password and confirm with a method you registered.
stepUp.managePasswordHint: To change your sign-in methods, enter your password again.
stepUp.managePasskeyHint: Your passkey is asked for after you confirm.
stepUp.noMethods: This needs a passkey or an authenticator app, and you have not registered one. Add one on the Security page in Settings.
stepUp.passkeyUnsupported: Your only method is a passkey, and this browser cannot use passkeys here. Use another browser or a recovery code from Settings.
stepUp.deviceCodeHint: Create the code on another device that has your passkey, under Settings → Security → Add a passkey on another device. If this device has your passkey, choose Use a passkey.

errors.wrongEither: The password or the second step was incorrect.
errors.passkeyFailed: The passkey could not be verified.
errors.passkeyNoUV: This passkey provider does not report user verification (PIN or biometrics), so the passkey was not added. In the browser's prompt, choose this device (such as Windows Hello) or a security key and try again.
errors.passkeyCanceled: The passkey check was canceled or timed out.
errors.passkeyDomain: Passkeys do not work at this address. Open the dashboard at its configured domain.
errors.passkeyUnavailable: Passkeys are not set up on this server.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Try again in {{remaining}}.
errors.unavailable: Your security settings cannot be read. Ask an administrator to reset them.
errors.manageExpired: The confirmation has expired. Try again.

recovery.title: Recovery codes
recovery.intro: Use one of these codes if you lose your passkey or phone. Each code works only once.
recovery.warning: You will not see these codes again. Copy them or write them down now.

deviceCode.title: Device code
deviceCode.intro: On the new device, open Settings → Security → Add a passkey, then enter your password and this code to confirm your identity.
deviceCode.expired: This code has expired. Create a new one if you still need it.

totp.title: Set up an authenticator app
totp.intro: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or enter the key, then type the 6-digit code it shows.
totp.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app

passkeyLogin.title: Turn on passkey sign-in
passkeyLogin.intro: Sign in on this browser with a passkey instead of your password. It works for {{days}} from the day you turn it on. Enter your password, then confirm with your passkey.
passkeyLogin.prfUnsupported: This passkey cannot use the PRF extension, so passkey sign-in was not turned on. Your passkey storage may not support PRF, or the passkey may have been added before this feature existed. Try adding the passkey again. You can still use it for two-step verification.
passkeyLogin.passwordTooLong: Your password is too long for passkey sign-in.
passkeyLogin.remember: Sign in with a passkey on this browser from now on
passkeyLogin.storageFailed: This browser's storage cannot be written, so passkey sign-in was not turned on. If this is a private window, try again in a normal window.

passkeys.addIntro: Name this passkey so you can tell it apart later, then follow your browser’s prompt.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.confirmIntro: To make sure the passkey works, you will use it once more. Follow your browser's prompts.
passkeys.leftoverSignaled: Your browser was asked to remove this passkey.
passkeys.leftoverManual: This passkey for {{rpId}} cannot be used. Remove it from your passkey provider.

viewer.empty: Open a file in the file explorer to see it here.
viewer.imageFailed: This image can't be shown. The browser may not support the format, or the file may be damaged.
viewer.mediaFailed: This file can't be played. The browser may not support its codec. Download it and open it in another program.
viewer.pdfFailed: This PDF can't be shown. Download it to open it.
viewer.binary: This file isn't text, so its contents can't be shown.
viewer.truncated: This file is large, so only the first {{size}} is shown.
viewer.security: This session needs a security check before previewing files.
